newsitem.title: UK: Germany says oil sale preparations on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Germany says oil sale preparations on schedule.

text.p: German oil supply agency EBV said on Monday that it would begin analysis in the middle of this week of the strategic crude stocks it has put up for sale to help lower its budget deficit.
A spokesman for the agency said the first of a series of tenders to run this year and next would proceed as planned next week.
The first tender is expected to be for some 450,000 cubic meters (2.8 million barrels).

"We have collected the oil in the Northwest Oil (NWO) pipeline and analysis will start in a couple of days," the spokesman said. "We will send out the tender early next week with the details of quality and quantity."
Bonn plans to sell more than 50 million barrels of crude in total or about 20 percent of national strategic reserves.
The crude is being pumped from salt caverns via the NWO pipeline to storage tanks at the German port of Wilhelmshaven.
Germany's economics ministry has said that the oil typically would be a mixture of 50 percent Iranian Heavy, 25 percent Arabian Light and 25 percent Iraqi Kirkuk.
